a319.speaker: Sports leaders and officials

a319.speaker: Workers in the city of Maputo
a319.name: Workers in the city of Maputo
a319.speech: Say it is challenging to work on a public holiday in order to earn their daily bread, speaking on the occasion of International Workers' Day.

a319.speaker: Minister of Labour, Gender and Social Action of Mozambique
a319.name: Minister of Labour
a319.title: Gender and Social Action of Mozambique
a319.speech: Says the growing labour disputes are consequences of the current economic situation the country is going through.

a319.speaker: Association of Small and Medium Enterprises of Mozambique
a319.name: Association of Small and Medium Enterprises of Mozambique
a319.speech: Points with satisfaction to the gradual resumption of activities by some companies.

a560.speaker: Ayele Hegena (PhD), director general for policy, law and standards research development at the Environment, Forest & Climate Change Commission
a560.name: Ayele Hegena (PhD)
a560.title: director general for policy, law and standards research development at the Environment, Forest & Climate Change Commission
a560.speech: Said lack of environmental technical expertise of both judges and prosecutors is one of the major difficulties for the effective enforcement of environmental laws in Ethiopia. "This led the courts to be reluctant to engage with environmental matters," Ayele told Fortune, "and prosecute violations that require the use of technical reports and scientific understanding."

a560.speaker: Ayele Hegena (PhD), director general for policy, law and standards research development at the Environment, Forest & Climate Change Commission
a560.name: Ayele Hegena (PhD)
a560.title: director general for policy, law and standards research development at the Environment, Forest & Climate Change Commission
a560.speech: Said the current police force does not have the knowledge nor the capacity to be entrusted with these cases; that the judges and all of the legal professionals under this establishment are expected to be vigilant and sensitive toward environmental issues and develop environmental law, compliance and enforcement consistency through the cases that come before the courts; and that as a start the green tribunal will be established at a federal level, with regional states able to form their own if they have the capacity.

a560.speaker: Andualem Mekonnen (PhD), environmentalist and assistant professor at the School of Natural Science, Addis Abeba University
a560.name: Andualem Mekonnen (PhD)
a560.title: environmentalist and assistant professor at the School of Natural Science, Addis Abeba University
a560.speech: Said that at a glance this might be deemed a profound move to address environmental issues, but it falls into doubt when looking at the capacity of the regulatory institutions; "Designing programmes or approaches just for the sake of being established will not solve the current environmental problems." "I highly doubt the execution of these kinds of programmes," he said. "Instead, the government should work on the grassroots issues from proper studies to proper assessments before jumping into anything."

a662.speaker: ActionAid International, report 'The Human Cost of Public Sector Cuts in Africa' (executive summary)
a662.name: ActionAid International
a662.title: report 'The Human Cost of Public Sector Cuts in Africa' (executive summary)
a662.speech: Says the research involved 616 individuals in rural and urban locations (296 health workers and teachers and 320 service users), which "reveals that a decline in the quality and availability of services has stretched frontline health workers and teachers thin, and threatened the rights of communities." ; "Health workers and teachers are facing overwhelming workloads and fewer resources to perform their jobs effectively, while communities are deprived of public services due to high costs and poor quality."

a662.speaker: ActionAid International, report 'The Human Cost of Public Sector Cuts in Africa' (recommendations)
a662.name: ActionAid International
a662.title: report 'The Human Cost of Public Sector Cuts in Africa' (recommendations)
a662.speech: Calls for immediate actions from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the governments of the six debt-ridden countries and their health and education ministries: "We urge the IMF to stop imposing austerity measures and privatisation, and focus instead on progressive tax reforms and debt relief or cancellation to increase government revenues for greater investment in public services." ; "National governments should reject coercive IMF policies, seek debt relief or cancellation, and expand tax revenues in fair ways to rebuild public health and education workforces and infrastructure." ; "They should demand the democratisation of decisions on debt relief and cancellation, with the creation of a UN Framework Convention on Sovereign Debt, and support the UN Framework Convention on Tax." ; "They should also prioritise the substantive gender equality commitments made in the groundbreaking Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action - 30 years old this year - by ensuring that women's rights are upheld in economic policy." ; "Education ministries should collaborate with finance ministries to ensure that at least 20% of national budgets are allocated to education, in line with global benchmarks. They should ensure there are sufficient numbers of trained and qualified teachers, who are fairly remunerated and have access to professional development and support to reduce the burden of unpaid care work that falls - particularly on women teachers." ; "There is also a need to ensure that schools are gender responsive and inclusive and to focus on increasing funding to build more schools, improve school infrastructure and ensure learning materials that are accessible for all learners including those with diverse needs." ; "Health ministries should work with finance ministries to ensure the achievement of the Abuja Declaration benchmark of allocating 15% of national budget towards healthcare." ; "They need to recruit more health workers, ensuring they are fairly remunerated, allocate more resources to public health facilities, improve healthcare infrastructure, and provide mental health support for workers."

a662.speaker: ActionAid International
a662.name: ActionAid International
a662.speech: Emphasises that the measures "aim to create a more equitable and effective public service system, in line with States' human rights obligations and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) - to serve the needs of communities better."

a662.speaker: ActionAid International survey of 616 health workers, teachers and service users in six African countries
a662.name: ActionAid International survey of 616 health workers
a662.title: teachers and service users in six African countries
a662.speech: Found that across the six countries 84% of all teachers surveyed reported a drop in real income of between 10% and 50% since 2020, while 97% of health workers describe their wages as insufficient to cover rent, food and household expenses; 70% of teachers and 85% of health workers feel overwhelmed; 89% of teachers and 95% of health workers report stress linked to financial instability and excessive workloads; 87% of teacher respondents cite a shortage of essential classroom furniture and reduced access to teaching materials and 73% of education sector workers have had to purchase resources themselves; 87% of health workers report a scarcity of medical equipment and supplies due to insufficient budgets, and 84% report severe shortages in staff.

a662.speaker: Community members/respondents surveyed by ActionAid
a662.name: Community members/respondents surveyed by ActionAid
a662.speech: Reported that women and girls are the most affected by rising health costs due to increased caregiving responsibilities, bearing the heaviest load and reduced access to maternal care ; women in urban areas report shouldering an additional 20 to 28 hours of care work each week, similar in rural households ; criticised government mismanagement and regressive taxation policies that under-tax the wealthiest individuals and corporations while over-taxing ordinary people.

a662.speaker: ActionAid International, report 'The Human Cost of Public Sector Cuts in Africa' (conclusion)
a662.name: ActionAid International
a662.title: report 'The Human Cost of Public Sector Cuts in Africa' (conclusion)
a662.speech: Concludes that public education and healthcare services are "plagued by staffing shortages, inadequate infrastructure, and financial barriers - leading to violations of people's rights to health and education" ; "Women and marginalised groups face the greatest burden, with increased unpaid care work and restricted access to essential services. There is an urgent need for reforms to end austerity, recruit more workers, pay them a living wage, upgrade infrastructure, and ensure health and education systems are gender-responsive." ; "The findings of this report point toward the detrimental impact of cuts in government spending on essential sectors, influenced by international financial institutions such as the IMF on the health and education sectors." ; "ActionAid calls for transformative change in how economic policy is governed internationally, and ensuring decisions are made inclusively and democratically, to ensure feminist and just alternatives, prioritise human rights, tax justice, climate justice, and value care over GDP growth."

a662.speaker: ActionAid International (background statement)
a662.name: ActionAid International (background statement)
a662.speech: Explains that for decades it has been at the forefront of research into the impact of IMF austerity recommendations in relation to public sector wage policies on spending on public services: "This research has highlighted the gendered impacts of austerity, and leads us to hold the IMF responsible for 50 years of failed economic policy, particularly in Africa." ; "We have also documented the impact of the growing debt crisis on health and education spending, their gendered impacts and the compounding effect of the climate crisis."

a675.speaker: Republic of Djibouti / Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI communiqué)
a675.name: Republic of Djibouti / Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI communiqué)
a675.speech: Welcomes the historic decision handed down by the International Court of Justice in the case brought by South Africa against Israel ; states that the decision, although it does not immediately impose a ceasefire under the provisional measures, "constitutes a decisive victory for humanity, for the international rule of law and for non-impunity" and a significant turning point in the quest for justice for the Palestinian people ; stresses the imperative of implementing fully and immediately the measures set out in the ruling, calls on the international community to assume its responsibilities to achieve a complete and comprehensive halt to Israeli aggression, and insists on the need to ensure immediate and sustained humanitarian aid in the Gaza Strip.

a675.speaker: Republic of Djibouti / Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI communiqué)
a675.name: Republic of Djibouti / Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI communiqué)
a675.speech: Expresses its profound gratitude to the Republic of South Africa for its honourable stance in favour of human rights and justice, and for having decided to bring this case before the International Court of Justice.

a763.speaker: Colonel Lamine Kapory Sanogo, Governor of Koulikoro
a763.name: Colonel Lamine Kapory Sanogo
a763.title: Governor of Koulikoro
a763.speech: Welcomed this active solidarity of the government towards its people.

a763.speaker: Beneficiaries of the rice distribution
a763.name: Beneficiaries of the rice distribution
a763.speech: Expressed wishes of happiness, prosperity and peace for Mali and for the Transition authorities.

a874.speaker: Prof. Paul Bosu, Director General of the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
a874.name: Prof. Paul Bosu
a874.title: Director General of the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
a874.speech: Assured the government of the commitment of the Council to support it to achieve the desired agricultural production level of the country ; noted, “CRI stands ready to partner the government and the development partners to revolutionise the agricultural landscape to enhance food security, jobs creation, youth development and improved livelihoods. We have the required technologies for this great transformation and are committed to work with government and development partners to achieve the Ghana that we all desire.”

a874.speaker: Dr. Caroline Makanto Sogbui, Director CORAF/IREACH Technical Advisor from Cameroon
a874.name: Dr. Caroline Makanto Sogbui
a874.title: Director CORAF/IREACH Technical Advisor from Cameroon
a874.speech: Said with the enviable track record of CRI in developing and releasing new crop technologies, realisation of the objectives of the Consortium is not in doubt ; “When you’re working with institutions like Crops Research Institute on development projects, you’re always happy. If all the partners can be like Crops Research Institute, you can sleep knowing that, at the end of the day, you’ll not have any problems because sometimes when you work with some institutions, you don’t know what the funds are being used for.”

a874.speaker: Yusif Bumbas, Consortium member farmer
a874.name: Yusif Bumbas
a874.title: Consortium member farmer
a874.speech: Expressed optimism about the success of the project.

a1000.speaker: Oxfam (NGO, press release)
a1000.name: Oxfam (NGO
a1000.title: press release)
a1000.speech: Denounced on Thursday France's "hypocrisy" over its development aid policy, hampered by budget cuts at a time when millions of French speakers "need emergency humanitarian aid" around the world ; "In view of the first documents of the 2025 budget bill, this text will surely bury all the efforts made by France on international solidarity since 2017, since it provides for a 1.3 billion euro drop in official development assistance" ; "This setback comes at a time when 70 million French speakers, the equivalent of the French population, today need emergency humanitarian aid," the NGO added, citing countries such as Senegal, Burkina Faso, Mali and the Democratic Republic of Congo ; "France seems to remain apathetic" in the face of deteriorating living conditions in poor countries, Oxfam also asserts, stating that France "provided only 1.7% of the humanitarian funding that French-speaking countries needed to cope with their crisis" in 2023.

a1000.speaker: Alan Anic, campaign and advocacy officer for international solidarity at Oxfam
a1000.name: Alan Anic
a1000.title: campaign and advocacy officer for international solidarity at Oxfam
a1000.speech: "Emmanuel Macron is pulling off one of his finest 'at the same time' moves, since he is bringing his counterparts together in Paris while withdrawing funding that is essential to their development," he denounces, quoted in a press release.

a1000.speaker: OECD statistics
a1000.name: OECD statistics
a1000.speech: According to OECD statistics, France's official development assistance (ODA) to poor countries fell in 2023 compared with the previous year, to 15.4 billion euros, representing 0.5% of Gross National Income (GNI).

a1120.speaker: Mahmoud Ma'alin Abdulle (Cabdulle), Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a1120.name: Mahmoud Ma'alin Abdulle (Cabdulle)
a1120.title: Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a1120.speech: Expressed his gratitude to the United States Government and USAID for their longstanding support in state building, development, and humanitarian assistance to the Somali people ; He highlighted the importance of this collaboration in fostering resilience and improving the livelihoods of communities across Somalia.

a1228.speaker: UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a1228.name: UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a1228.speech: has urged an immediate end to hostilities and restoration of calm in Morobo and Yei counties, Central Equatoria State, following renewed clashes between government forces and the SPLA-IO that displaced thousands of civilians in the region.

a1228.speaker: Charles Data Bullen, Morobo County Commissioner
a1228.name: Charles Data Bullen
a1228.title: Morobo County Commissioner
a1228.speech: said on Thursday that more than 7,000 internally displaced persons who fled fighting in the area are in dire need of humanitarian assistance, and that the IDPs who fled the clashes between government forces and opposition forces in Panyume and Bulumbi payams are sheltering in schools and churches.

a1228.speaker: Priyanka Chowdhury, UNMISS Spokesperson
a1228.name: Priyanka Chowdhury
a1228.title: UNMISS Spokesperson
a1228.speech: in a statement shared with Eye Radio urged all military actors to refrain from conflict and prioritize the protection of civilians, and warned that the escalating violence is deepening South Sudan’s already fragile political and security landscape, placing civilian lives in serious jeopardy ; “UNMISS is deeply concerned by reports of clashes between the South Sudan People’s Defense Forces and Sudan People’s Liberation Army-in Opposition in Morobo and Yei counties, which have led to civilian displacement and casualties,” ; “The Mission calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities and restoration of calm, given already fragile political and security conditions in the country.”

a1228.speaker: UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a1228.name: UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a1228.speech: further appealed to the warring factions to refrain from conflict, prioritize the protection of civilians, resolve differences through dialogue, while ensuring unimpeded access for peacekeepers to reinforce security.

a1228.speaker: UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a1228.name: UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a1228.speech: added that it is engaging with authorities, security actors, faith-based groups, traditional leaders, youths, civil society and community leaders to prevent the situation from deteriorating.

a1281.speaker: Sean Jones, Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.name: Sean Jones
a1281.title: Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.speech: On his plans: "I believe USAID is here because we have things to offer. America wants friends and partners like Ethiopia. The best ideas, resources and some of our capacity to help Ethiopia through this historic period of time that Ethiopia needs right now. Right now there are many reforms underway that are more focused on democratic values and systems, so our support will be helping Ethiopia in the upcoming election by supporting the election board, we also want to support substantially and the economic reform agenda of the government in line with American values we also need to support the people who need food assistance and humanitarian assistance and crisis response."

a1281.speaker: Sean Jones, Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.name: Sean Jones
a1281.title: Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.speech: On healthcare: "There is a commitment to stop the spread of HIV. We also want to help alleviate tuberculosis and malaria, we want to continue that, we are not dramatically changing, our level of investment to maintain the gains that Ethiopia has made with HIV in particular, the cases have dropped substantially thanks to the tremendous support and commitment of the Ethiopian government to ensure that the case load is down and identifying new cases very quickly by working with the targeted populations." ; On tuberculosis: "We signed a MOU to continue working with the Ministry of Health. The health system is sufficiently strong now so we are working with civil society organizations."

a1281.speaker: Sean Jones, Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.name: Sean Jones
a1281.title: Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.speech: On the FITIH justice reform programme: "This program helps protect the rights of citizens and updates the justice system. We are working with the Attorney General and the Ministry of Peace to strengthen the way that it engages with the public to review laws that may need updating and provide additional capacity for Ethiopia's lawyers, judges and prosecutors. It has some focus on capacity building and how to technically implement Ethiopia's vision."

a1281.speaker: Sean Jones, Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.name: Sean Jones
a1281.title: Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.speech: On the electoral board: "Outside of the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE), we are helping civil society organizations and citizens to engage with NEBE to provide advice, on how to conduct free and fair elections." ; On whether the election will be held on schedule: "It is the government's decision but we want to ensure NEBE is as strong as possible for the election. It is a lot of organization, a lot of people, a lot of things have to happen. NEBE is one part of that. The other is the government ensuring security."

a1281.speaker: Sean Jones, Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.name: Sean Jones
a1281.title: Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.speech: On the private sector and the Jigjiga meat processing plant: "I just have had the opportunity to talk with the general manager, owner and founder of the factory, he closed it temporarily and wants to have another project in that area to grow food for the livestock. Actually he is increasing investment in that area so that he can have a long consistent supply for the factory, that is a tremendous support for the country and I am proud of the investors working in that region investing substantial money. More broadly our investment in the private sector is very important like now, we have had private sector involvement for a long time but it hasn't been strong necessarily as it could be. A robust private sector will do wonders for economic growth." ; "In policy we are working with government officials on reforms to help the private sector. We are working to help businesspeople and farmers to access finance, we are also working with financial institutions so business can access land and resources."

a1281.speaker: Sean Jones, Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.name: Sean Jones
a1281.title: Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.speech: On agriculture and seeds: "We want to help Ethiopia have less reliance on external factors to grow, produce and sell food while making sure that the crops are healthy." ; "The US government basis this on the needs of the country, not every country desires hybrid seeds, not every country needs genetically modified seeds... we do believe that every country should make their own decisions regarding what types of seeds and technologies and approaches they want to bring to their local market." ; "One is seed varieties. This could be local seeds, weather controlling pests and other pests' like fungus, or it could be the introduction of hybrid seeds that are outside of Ethiopia we work with as well, and when Ethiopia's ready, in a position to have genetically produced seeds or other types of seed technologies we support that, we are not pushing to do that right now we want to have Ethiopian farmers help to have access to seed varieties."

a1281.speaker: Sean Jones, Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.name: Sean Jones
a1281.title: Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.speech: On the allegation that USAID funds seed shops selling only its own products: "So that is not accurate. I appreciate that because I can help correct it, we went into partnership with a company called Dow DuPont which changed their name to Corteva, what we did is we introduced tens of thousands of farmers to new products that were legally brought by this company and also other companies. We didn't fund them, this is done by the private sector, we encouraged them to use better products." ; On dependency on certain fertilizers: "That is true in general not specific to Corteva, if seed technology has patent rights, and a lot of seed technology doesn't germinate every year, that is true. I think that is farmers' decision whether they can continue or use local seeds even hybrid varieties where they do germinate every year. They can see higher production yield and a higher rate of protection in their farming."

a1281.speaker: Sean Jones, Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.name: Sean Jones
a1281.title: Mission Director of USAID Ethiopia
a1281.speech: On economic reform: "This is a new area in our assistance program in Ethiopia, again we are really proud to be invited to provide assistance to the Ministry of Finance, the Prime Minster and the Central Bank. We have brought in a very famous economist and signed a three-year contract and his team from Harvard University to provide advice to the very capable people here the Ethiopian people are leading this reform effort they came and provide assessment, and diagnostics. Particularly it is a critical period for Ethiopia and Ethiopia's economy." ; "They didn't come and start offering advice for them; there are also a bunch of Ethiopian teams that travel here and back to Harvard University in the US. They give advice considering global perspectives, and bring some of the best ideas. It is a conversation between really brilliant people there in Addis Ababa leading reforms and people from Harvard." ; "We have a lot of projects focused on helping the Ethiopian people one thing about USAID is that we are invited here and we are proud to be a partner of the people and government."

a1511.speaker: United States Marshals Service (USMS) (media release posted on its X handle)
a1511.name: United States Marshals Service (USMS) (media release posted on its X handle)
a1511.speech: Said Abreu was arrested on Tuesday, April 2, on multiple warrants from Massachusetts ; According to the release, he was wanted on one count of homicide, one count of unlawful possession of a firearm, one count of unlawful possession of a loaded firearm, one count of unlawful possession of ammunition, one count of assault & battery with a deadly weapon, one count of discharging a firearm within 500ft of a building, and one count of assault & battery (domestic) ; The release noted that Abreu was being sought in connection to a homicide which occurred in Brockton, MA on Sunday, March 31, 2024 ; "The USMS, District of Massachusetts Fugitive Task Force, provided investigative leads to the USMS MVOTF requesting assistance in locating and apprehending Abreu in Maine. Through a collaborative law enforcement effort, authorities developed information which led investigators to Lewiston, ME. USMS Task Force members and the Lewiston Maine Police were able to identify Abreu in a motor vehicle and were able to safely apprehend him without incident in Lewiston, Maine. Abreu is charged as a Fugitive from Justice and will be arraigned in Maine pending his extradition back to Massachusetts. The USMS, Maine Violent Offender Task Force received significant assistance from the Lewiston, ME Police Department, the USMS District of MA Fugitive Task Force, the Massachusetts State Police Violent Fugitive Apprehension Section (VFAS), and the Brockton, MA Police Department. The USMS Maine Violent Offender Task Force is comprised of members of the U.S. Marshals Service, Maine Department of Corrections, Biddeford Police Department, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection. If you have any information regarding the whereabouts of any State or Federal Fugitive please contact the United States Marshals Service, District of Maine at MED.TIPLINE@usdoj."

a1511.speaker: United States Marshals Service (USMS), Maine Violent Offender Task Force (MVOTF)
a1511.name: United States Marshals Service (USMS)
a1511.title: Maine Violent Offender Task Force (MVOTF)
a1511.speech: Has announced the arrest of a wanted fugitive, Jeremiah Abreu, 20, of Brockton, MA in Lewiston, Maine.

a1708.speaker: International Energy Agency (IEA)
a1708.name: International Energy Agency (IEA)
a1708.speech: According to the IEA, only about 20% of Liberia's population has access to electricity.

a1708.speaker: Siezie Siefa, emerging analyst in Project Management in energy and infrastructure development in Liberia (author of the paper)
a1708.name: Siezie Siefa
a1708.title: emerging analyst in Project Management in energy and infrastructure development in Liberia (author of the paper)
a1708.speech: Argues that managing national energy infrastructures in Liberia requires a multifaceted approach with a strong emphasis on financing, project management, risk mitigation, and the adoption of sustainable energy solutions, and proposes a framework to address these challenges ; notes that the African Development Bank, World Bank, USAID, the European Union, GIZ and other multilateral agencies play critical roles in financing Liberia's energy projects, but that it is essential for Liberia to explore diverse financing mechanisms such as public-private partnerships, green and climate finance, donor funding and domestic revenue generation ; warns that political instability, corruption, weak institutional capacity, low creditworthiness and exchange-rate volatility hinder investment, and that Liberia must transition to renewable energy sources including hydropower, solar, and biomass to achieve long-term energy security.

a1835.speaker: US Mission in Nigeria (post under its #TransparencyTuesday campaign)
a1835.name: US Mission in Nigeria (post under its #TransparencyTuesday campaign)
a1835.speech: Shared the report and stated that "While Nigerians are urged to endure economic hardship like labor pains, some governors are splurging billions on new government houses, airports, and flyovers that may not be necessary."

a1835.speaker: Chief Femi Fani-Kayode, former Nigerian Minister of Aviation
a1835.name: Chief Femi Fani-Kayode
a1835.title: former Nigerian Minister of Aviation
a1835.speech: Accused the U.S. government of hypocrisy and urged it to fix its internal problems before lecturing others on governance; said America is aiding genocide through its continued support of Israel, writing on X: "Whilst the children of Gaza are being slaughtered and starved, the American government is sending more and more weapons to Israel to assist them in committing genocide." ; "Worse still, the American government is using the Ukraine-Russia war to launder money and make billions of dollars for its corrupt leaders." ; accused the U.S. of having used USAID as a conduit to fund billions of dollars into and from various nations across the world in a bid to "corrupt and destroy them": "And up until Trump came, the US used USAID as a conduit to fund billions of dollars into and from various nations all over the world in order to corrupt and destroy them" ; said the U.S. government has no moral standing to give lessons on governance to other nations: "Before you give us lessons in governance, kindly drain your American swamp and clean up the mess you have put the world in."
